title: Halting from Equal Register States
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}\colon\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $l$ be a label of the program $A(E)$. If register states $\mathrm{st}$ and $\mathrm{st}'$ are equal and the machine started at label $l$ with the register vector of $\mathrm{st}'$ and no answer halts with answer $r\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ after finitely many steps, with every earlier configuration satisfying the program’s safety condition and all register values at most $B$, then it also halts with answer $r$ from label $l$ with the register vector of $\mathrm{st}$ and no answer, under those same conditions.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is an oracle on four indices and Boolean words
there is a finite guarded halting execution from $(l,\mathrm{st}'.toV,\mathrm{none})$ with answer $r$
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle on four families of
binary words, let $x$ be a binary word, and let $l$ be a program label. If two register
states $\mathrm{st}$ and $\mathrm{st}'$ are equal and $A(E)$, started at label $l$ with
the register vector of $\mathrm{st}'$ and no answer, halts with answer
$r\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ after a finite execution whose earlier
configurations satisfy the safety conditions and have all registers at most $B$, then it
also halts with answer $r$ from the register vector of $\mathrm{st}$.
